title: Execution of a subtraction routine
statement: Let $a,b,f,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $m\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $o$ assign a Boolean to each of five indices and each finite Boolean string, and let $y$ be a finite Boolean string. For any subtraction site $k$ and register configuration $st$ whose fifteen registers are at most $B$, the register program starting at the phase-zero instruction for $k$, with register values given by $st$ and no answer recorded, reaches its exit instruction. At the endpoint, the register associated with $k$ is zero and the index register has value $\max(st.i-st_{r},0)$, where $st_r$ is the initial value of the register associated with $k$; every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the program's preconditions and has all register values at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: Oracle on five indices and finite Boolean strings
Initial register configuration $st$ has all fifteen values at most $B$
Execution starts at phase zero for $k$, with register values $st$ and no answer recorded
replaced:
Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $mode$ be a Boolean, let $o$ be an oracle
assigning a Boolean to each of five indices and each finite Boolean string, and let $y$
be a finite Boolean string. For any subtraction site $k$ and register state $st$ whose
fifteen natural-number registers are all at most $B$, the program starting at the
initial phase for $k$, with register values given by $st$ and no answer recorded,
reaches the exit phase for $k$ with the register associated to $k$ set to zero and the
index register set to $st.i$ minus the initial value of the register associated to $k$
(with subtraction truncated at zero). At every earlier configuration, all registers are
at most $B$ and the program's required preconditions hold.
